description:
The plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics: final accuracy, the difference in accuracy, and initial accuracy. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, with tick labels incrementing by 0.01. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy” and has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels incrementing by 0.2.  

The blue line, representing “Final Accuracy,” is plotted with circular markers and error bars, and it begins at approximately 0.92 at an initial confidence of 0.81, fluctuates between approximately 0.84 and 0.93, and ends at approximately 0.94 at an initial confidence of 0.99. The orange line, representing “Δ Accuracy,” is plotted with square markers and error bars, starting at approximately 0.44 at an initial confidence of 0.81, declining to approximately 0.08 at an initial confidence of 0.97, and ending at approximately 0.05 at an initial confidence of 0.99. The green line, representing “Initial Accuracy,” is plotted with square markers and error bars, beginning at approximately 0.58 at an initial confidence of 0.81, gradually increasing to approximately 0.96 at an initial confidence of 0.99.
